answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like a crystal bond that is clear to verify and costly to break. A fake island of thousands of sock-puppet agents would then need to fund every identity, so the attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. The ripple effect is that cheap identity creation stops paying: the attacker must risk real capital per fake agent, and slashing removes that capital when peers attest to the fraud.
